The player places his resistance agents on spaces around town to achieve his goals – blowing up trains, publishing underground newspapers – but at the same time Milice collaborators and Wehrmacht soldiers patrol the area. Agents who can’t make it back to the safe house at the end of the day are arrested, and never seen again. [Rating: 1/10] The rating is for the kickstarter campaign and not the game, but worth mentioning.  Im still waiting for it and yet it is being sold for 30% cheaper at BGB.  Never back this company again!

[Rating: 1/10] A chore to play. Abysmal gameplay, spend your time walking on eggs and achieving nothing, fiddly in that most of the gameplay is actually browsing through the discard pile and the rulebook to see the odds of instantly losing on your next move. The least fun "game" I have touched since Finished.

[Rating: 1/10] Hate the commercial process: * Core box contains 50% of the extension (27€) but half the game. * Extensions contains 4 cards 3 City tokens So it is a 50% game + useless content,  with 4 carts + 3 tokens for 7.5 € so 7-6=1  Even the rule consider the extension as the "normal" game. This is an horrible commercial way to force us to buy the extension. Nothing justify the fact to split the game like this for 4 cards & 3 tokens as the extension cames out at the same time in store.  If all sellers starts  to sell games by 50% parts, i ll stop buying half-products.

[Rating: 3/10] Interesting setting, but there are too few strategic options and none of them matter if you get an unlucky card draw.

[Rating: 3/10] I'm sorry, I just don't get it. I gave it multiple chances, but all I see is uninteresting resource puzzle and getting screwed by random patrols.

[Rating: 3/10] Maquis has many strengths, but its few weaknesses undercut the overall experience. The variable objectives inject a great deal of variability and greatly influence the relevance of the different locations. Unfortunately, the early game openings seem rote and uninteresting (ie. you generally always need a second safe house). There is a satisfying opportunity cost with the worker placement though. You can put your workers in useful locations, but then risk patrol interference, or essentially waste workers to safe guard an escape route. [Rating: 3/10] Ok game at first but then feels like I’m just solving the same kind of puzzle over and over again. Burnout factor is high for me on this one.

[Rating: 3/10] Might be a good game here but boy, the rules are poorly written.  Very difficult to feel certain you are playing correctly - and the game isn't that complicated.

[Rating: 3.6/10] Maquis didn't live up to expectations. The luck factor outweighs most of the strategy, and there's a repetitiveness that reveals itself after multiple plays (even with variable Mission Cards). The production is impressive and there are some cool ideas here, but that's not enough for me.  Read my comprehensive review: https://shelfgamer.com/review-maquis/
